title: trqp: long Content-Length crashes handler on 3.11+
description: git-vouch-trqp:334-335. 'int(length) > MAX_BODY' runs on any all-digit header. Since Python 3.11 (and patched 3.9/3.10 security releases), int() of a string over 4300 digits raises ValueError (sys.int_info.str_digits_check_threshold). Header lines may be up to 64 KiB. Reproduced on 3.12: 'Content-Length: ' + '9'*5000 drops the connection with no reply, and stderr gets a socketserver traceback (ValueError: Exceeds the limit (4300 digits)). What goes wrong: the documented contract (a 400 malformedRequest for any bad Content-Length, test_bad_content_length_is_malformed) breaks, and anyone can spray tracebacks into the operator log. Fix: bound the length before converting, e.g. 'not (length.isascii() and length.isdigit()) or len(length) > 6 or int(length) > MAX_BODY'. Test: add '9'*5000 to the test_bad_content_length_is_malformed parameters.
close_reason: duplicate of vouch-s9w2.8 (filed concurrently; reproduced on 3.12 with 5000 digits, also fails on patched 3.9/3.10)
